expectations.text: Defines the deemed export rule: releasing ITAR technical data to a foreign person in the US is an export to their country/countries of nationality
expectations.evidence: "releasing technical data to a foreign person... is treated as an export to that person's country of nationality (or countries of nationality, if dual national), even if the release happens entirely inside the United States".

expectations.text: States a license/authorization (e.g., DSP-5) is required unless an exemption applies, judged as if exporting to that nationality
expectations.evidence: "you have committed an unauthorized export unless an exemption applies"; authorization paths: "A DDTC export license or agreement (e.g., a Technical Assistance Agreement)"; "exemptions under 22 CFR 126.18".

expectations.text: Covers what counts as release: visual access, oral disclosure, physical access to hardware revealing technical data, IT system access
expectations.evidence: "whether by showing a document, verbal briefing, granting system/network access, allowing them to observe a controlled process"; "Granting network/file-share access... CAD/PLM system access".

expectations.text: Recommends a Technology Control Plan: access controls, segregated systems, badging/escort, training, screening of nationalities against §126.1
expectations.evidence: "Implement a Technology Control Plan... physical and IT access segmentation (badge access, network permissions...)"; "Train program managers"; "employee isn't from a proscribed country (126.1 list)"; "Screen for 126.18 disqualifiers".

expectations.text: Notes dual/third nationalities considerations and that US persons include green-card holders (foreign person = not US citizen/permanent resident/protected person)
expectations.evidence: "foreign person... includes anyone who is not a U.S. citizen, U.S. lawful permanent resident (green card holder), or a protected individual under 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)"; dual nationals noted ("countries of nationality, if dual national").
